recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The current specification already implements the FHIR-19745 decision when read with the later published eld-19/eld-20 clarification issues; any future change to eld-20's warning expression or logical-model behavior should be handled as a separate work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-19745 was a Published FHIR-core change request resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked that the eld-19 regular expression be corrected so the 64-character path component limit is actually enforced, that eld-19 mention that enforcement, and that eld-20 not imply it is the hard length rule.
initial_application: The anchoring portion appears to have been applied by the later FHIR-26306 technical-correction commit 6c40cfa8f4, which added ^/$ anchors and fixed XPath namespace/escaping for eld-19 and eld-20. The FHIR-19745-tagged commit 913853e2d9 updated source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml so eld-19 mentioned the 64-character maximum and the eld-20 expression family used a bounded naming regex.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini as a current datatype/page and normative artifact. Later Published issues FHIR-25627, FHIR-38795, and FHIR-38796 clarified that eld-19 carries the hard 64-character rule while eld-20 is naming-convention guidance with a logical-model caveat; those related issues are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current eld-19 is an error rule whose description and anchored FHIRPath/XPath regex enforce {1,64} for each '.'-separated ElementDefinition.path component, while eld-20 describes UpperCamelCase/lowerCamelCase warning semantics and no longer carries the stale hard length-limit description.
